en: Dark, towering cumulonimbus clouds often form over Manila during hot afternoons, signaling an impending thunderstorm.
Clay soil feels sticky when wet and forms hard clods when dry, unlike loose sandy soil.
Pumice is a light-colored volcanic rock that contains so many gas holes it can float on water.
Morning dew on grass blades forms when water vapor in the cool night air condenses.
Venus appears as the exceptionally bright Morning Star in the eastern sky just before sunrise.
The North Star, Polaris, stays in a fixed position in the northern night sky while other stars appear to move.
A total lunar eclipse turns the full moon a reddish color when Earth blocks direct sunlight.
Lahars are fast-moving mudflows composed of volcanic ash and rainwater that travel down river channels after eruptions.
Storm surges are abnormal rises in seawater pushed ashore by strong typhoon winds, flooding coastal areas.
Rainbows form a circular arc in the sky when sunlight refracts and reflects inside suspended raindrops.
Obsidian is a naturally occurring volcanic glass that breaks with very sharp, smooth edges.
Sheet erosion visibly removes the dark, nutrient-rich topsoil layer from sloping farmlands during heavy rains.
